body: Only one who loves can remember so well.
author: Anton Chekhov

body: Everyone has the same God; only people differ.
author: Anton Chekhov

body: Man will only become better when you make him see what he is like.
author: Anton Chekhov

body: No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted.
author: Aesop

body: Betray a friend, and you'll often find you have ruined yourself.
author: Aesop

body: A doubtful friend is worse than a certain enemy. Let a man be one thing or the other, and we then know how to meet him.
author: Aesop

body: Never trust the advice of a man in difficulties.
author: Aesop

body: A liar will not be believed even when he speaks the truth.
author: Aesop

body: After all is said and done, more is said than done.
author: Aesop

body: It is easy to be brave at a safe distance.
author: Aesop

body: The smaller the mind, the greater the conceit.
author: Aesop

body: Fine clothes may disguise, but silly words will disclose a fool.
author: Aesop

body: Please all, and you will please none.
author: Aesop

body: Those who cry the loudest are not always the ones who are hurt the most.
author: Aesop

body: United we stand; divided we fall.
author: Aesop

body: Necessity is the mother of invention.
author: Aesop

body: Adversity tests the sincerity of friends.
author: Aesop

body: We often give our enemies the means for our own destruction.
author: Aesop

body: Wise men say nothing in dangerous times.
author: Aesop

body: A crust eaten in peace is better than a banquet partaken in anxiety.
author: Aesop

body: Any excuse will serve a tyrant.
author: Aesop

body: Appearances often are deceiving.
author: Aesop

body: Do not count your chickens before they are hatched.
author: Aesop

body: Everywhere man blames nature and fate yet his fate is mostly but the echo of his character and passion, his mistakes and his weaknesses.
author: Democritus

body: Nothing exists except atoms and empty space; everything else is opinion.
author: Democritus

body: Many much-learned men have no intelligence.
author: Democritus

body: By desiring little, a poor man makes himself rich.
author: Democritus

body: Everything existing in the universe is the fruit of chance and necessity.
author: Democritus

body: To a wise and good man the whole earth is his fatherland.
author: Democritus

body: Do not trust all men, but trust men of worth; the former course is silly, the latter a mark of prudence.
author: Democritus

body: Good means not merely not to do wrong, but rather not to desire to do wrong.
author: Democritus

body: No power and no treasure can outweigh the extension of our knowledge.
author: Democritus

body: It is greed to do all the talking but not to want to listen at all.
author: Democritus

body: Medicine heals diseases of the body, wisdom frees the soul from passions.
author: Democritus

body: Immoderate desire is the mark of a child, not a man.
author: Democritus

body: Education is an ornament for the prosperous, a refuge for the unfortunate.
author: Democritus

body: It is hard to fight desire; but to control it is the sign of a reasonable man.
author: Democritus
